topic.title: Second 47 Disclosure
topic.claim: Every 'get ready with me' reel buries the paid partnership tag around the 47th second, right after the hook and the outfit reveal.
topic.behaviour: Creators flash 'ad' in small text after they've already got you watching, just before the link in bio.
topic.mechanism: The disclosure exists to satisfy the platform's rule, not to actually tell you upfront what you're watching.
topic.why_now: this pattern has basically become the default across creator ads

score.why: Named, funny, deflates influencer marketing exactly the way she already believes nobody's really measuring the pitch.

topic.send_to: the friend who watches every GRWM reel

edits: slide 1: cut 'Technically disclosed. Practically invisible.' It's a mirrored-pair punchline. Keep 'It shows up once you're already hooked.' as the ending.
slide 1: the opener 'Every GRWM reel follows the same script now:' is flat. Try a plainer opinion first, like 'The paid partnership tag in GRWM reels is timed, not hidden.' Keep the list after it.
caption: 'latest point you've ever spotted' reads awkwardly. Use 'What's the latest second you've ever spotted the ad tag in a reel?'

paragraphs:
The GRWM reel is an ad that makes you wait for it:
- Hook
- Messy bun, bad lighting, "guys I'm so late"
- Outfit reveal
- "Okay so this serum..."
- Link in bio
The "Paid partnership" label was there from second one. Small and grey, right under her name.
Nobody reads it. That's what the messy bun is for.

draft.caption: Somewhere a brand manager is very proud of second 47.
draft.alt_text: A single text post listing the usual order of a get ready with me reel: hook, messy bun, outfit reveal, a product pitch, a tiny paid partnership tag that flashes by, then link in bio. It ends by saying the tag appears only after you're hooked.
